title: Enzyme Kinetics Michaelis-Menten 3D Simulator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive 3D Michaelis-Menten enzyme kinetics simulator.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x0a0a1a) with subtle ambient light (0x334466, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from position (5, 10, 7).
- Camera at position (0, 8, 18) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- A 3D reaction chamber: a semi-transparent (opacity 0.15) cylinder (radius 6, height 8) centered at origin, wireframe=false, with a subtle blue tint (0x2244aa).

## Molecular Entities
- Enzyme (E): Represented as green (0x22cc44) icosahedron geometries (radius 0.5). Start with 5 enzymes placed randomly inside the chamber.
- Substrate (S): Represented as orange (0xff8833) sphere geometries (radius 0.3). Start with 20 substrates placed randomly inside the chamber.
- Enzyme-Substrate Complex (ES): When E and S collide (distance < 1.0), they merge into a larger dodecahedron (radius 0.7, color 0xeeee22). The ES complex persists for a duration determined by 1/kcat before converting.
- Product (P): After ES complex breaks down, produce a purple (0xaa33ff) tetrahedron (radius 0.35) and release the enzyme back.
- All molecules should have gentle random Brownian motion inside the chamber (random velocity perturbations each frame, speed scaled by a temperature factor).
- Molecules must stay within the cylindrical boundary (bounce off walls).

## Kinetic Parameters (adjustable via UI)
- Vmax: range 0.5 to 5.0, default 2.0 (controls kcat = Vmax / [E_total])
- Km: range 1.0 to 20.0, default 5.0 (Michaelis constant, affects binding probability)
- Temperature factor: range 0.5 to 3.0, default 1.0 (scales Brownian motion speed)
- The binding probability when E and S are close should be proportional to ([S] / (Km + [S])) * dt_factor.
- The catalytic rate kcat = Vmax / totalEnzymes. ES complexes convert to P + E after a timer of 1/kcat seconds.

## UI / HUD
- Top-left panel with sliders for Vmax, Km, and Temperature, each with a numeric label showing current value.
- A 'Reset Simulation' button that restores initial counts (5 E, 20 S, 0 ES, 0 P) and clears all timers.
- An 'Add Substrate (+10)' button that spawns 10 new substrate spheres.
- Top-right real-time stats panel showing: Enzyme count, Substrate count, ES Complex count, Product count, Reaction Rate (products formed per second, computed as rolling average over last 3 seconds), and Elapsed Time in seconds.
- Bottom-center: a 2D overlay canvas (400x200) drawing a real-time Michaelis-Menten curve plot. X-axis = [S] (substrate concentration), Y-axis = reaction rate v. Plot the theoretical curve v = Vmax*[S]/(Km+[S]) as a white line, and overlay the current measured ([S], rate) as a red dot.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- enzymeCount: number of free enzymes
- substrateCount: number of free substrates
- complexCount: number of ES complexes
- productCount: number of products
- totalMolecules: enzymeCount + substrateCount + complexCount*2 + productCount (conservation check: should always equal initialE + initialS + productCount, since each ES uses 1 E + 1 S)
- vmax: current Vmax slider value
- km: current Km slider value
- temperature: current temperature slider value
- reactionRate: measured products per second (rolling 3s window)
- theoreticalRate: Vmax * [S] / (Km + [S]) where [S] = substrateCount
- elapsedTime: seconds since simulation start (paused during reset)
- simRunning: boolean, true when simulation is active
- lastResetTime: timestamp of last reset
- conservationValid: boolean, true if enzyme conservation holds (free E + ES complexes === initial enzyme count always)
- initialEnzymeCount: the starting enzyme count (5)
- initialSubstrateCount: the total substrates ever added (starts 20, increases by 10 per add)
- moleculePositions: array of {type, x, y, z} for all active molecules
- plotDataPoints: array of {s, v} measured data points recorded every 2 seconds

## Animation
- Use requestAnimationFrame. Each frame: update Brownian motion, check collisions for binding, update ES timers, convert expired ES to P+E, update stats, update plot.
- Molecules should glow slightly using emissive properties on their materials.
physics_constraints: Enzyme conservation law: free_enzymes + ES_complexes must always equal initial_enzyme_count (5). Mass conservation: enzymeCount + substrateCount + 2*complexCount + productCount must equal initialEnzymeCount + initialSubstrateCount. All molecules must remain within the cylindrical chamber boundary (radius 6, height 8). Brownian motion velocities scale linearly with temperature factor. Reaction rate must approach Vmax asymptotically as [S] increases. Km represents the substrate concentration at which rate = Vmax/2. No NaN values in any position or count fields.
